newsitem.title: VIETNAM: Vietnam targets 11 pct interest in T-bill sale.
newsitem.headline: Vietnam targets 11 pct interest in T-bill sale.

text.p: Vietnam will hold its first treasury bill sale of the year on Wednesday, with a target interest rate of 11 percent, an official at the central State Bank said on Monday.
The official said 30 billion dong ($2.68 million) worth of one year bills would be up for auction.
"It's the first time we've announced a target interest rate, so we're waiting to see what happens," the official said.

Treasury analysts told Reuters potential buyers would need clarification of a recent decision to withdraw tax exemption on interest income from treasury paper before deciding whether the target interest rate was attractive.

Vietnam sold some 906.4 billion ($81 million) worth of bills last year but the last auction in December failed to attract buyers, chiefly because bids were coming in at higher interest levels than the Finance Ministry was prepared to accept.
Traders said this was a result of tightened liquidity in the money market stemming from State Bank moves to engineer a gradual depreciation of the local currency.
At the last successful auction on November 27 Vietnam sold 2.5 billion dong worth of six month T-bills at an annual coupon of 8.2 percent. (US$1=11,186 dong)
